answer: Each agent must stake a yarrow-marked bond and maintain a public thread of signed work receipts. Peers cross-link these receipts into a shared trellis, so a sybil identity must fake months of consistent history across many nodes. Faking one thread costs real compute and stake slashing, while forging the full trellis multiplies that cost per identity, making mass sybils economically irrational.
